title: Parkfield House redevelopment brings 20 homes and an 80-bed care home to Middleton
body:
Muller Property Group says it has secured approval for 20 townhouses and an 80-bed care home at the former Parkfield House site off Manchester Old Road. The scheme reuses a three-acre brownfield site and involves demolition of the former Chubb Locks headquarters.

The building is identified as a non-designated heritage asset. That creates a local heritage issue, but is not the same as demolishing a nationally listed building. The planning decision should explain how the loss was balanced against the public benefits.

The townhouses are described as two- to four-bedroom properties. A secured affordable allocation, sale/rental split and current price list have not been verified. Care accommodation is a different housing product, with fees and support arrangements that should be explained separately.

Eighty care-home beds cannot simply be added to twenty houses and advertised as one hundred ordinary family homes. Any contribution to the housing-delivery measure must use the applicable treatment of communal accommodation.

Access, staff and visitor travel, drainage and the relationship with nearby services are central infrastructure questions. No site-specific capacity assessment was verified here. The developer’s approval statement does not supply that evidence.

No verified adverse builder finding relating to this Middleton scheme was established. A planning dispute elsewhere, or a similarly named company, would not alone establish a problem with this development.

Location: Manchester Old Road, Middleton

Planning stage: Developer reports detailed planning approval; reference 23/00335/FUL

Homes: 20 townhouses; 80 care-home beds reported separately

Let or for sale: Townhouse sale/rental and affordable split unknown; care fees unconfirmed

Land: Three-acre brownfield former headquarters site

Final planning agreement: Muller reports detailed approval, reference 23/00335/FUL. The complete executed deed, conditions and any variations were not verified.

Exact rents / prices: Exact townhouse prices/rents, estate charges and care-home fees have not been established from the reviewed official records or project announcement.

Affordable breakdown: 20 townhouses; no secured affordable count or tenure breakdown verified. The 80 care beds are a separate product and not 80 ordinary family homes.

Funded school capacity: No scheme-specific funded additional school places, named capital project and opening date were established from the accessible official records reviewed.

Funded healthcare capacity: A proposed care home is not evidence of funded GP or NHS capacity. Operator arrangements, NHS commissioning and any extra primary-care capacity were not established.

Funded transport capacity: No complete scheme-specific transport funding schedule or evidence of delivered service capacity was established from the accessible official records reviewed. Highway conditions and marketing descriptions do not establish funded bus or rail services.

The outstanding details identified above are not yet available to Rochdale Daily. This article will be updated when the information becomes available.

Research checked 14 October 2026. Advertised prices are snapshots, not achieved sale prices.

Read the borough-wide housing investigation and the other developments: https://rochdaledaily.co.uk/articles/rochdale-housing-developments-affordability-schools-gp-transport.html
